query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official dataset/API/search/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains PENDING_RAW_RESPONSE until candidate-specific area/location/address/record evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: ONS mid-year estimates are authoritative current demographic context. Candidate use requires exact current local-authority/geography binding; an authority total is not a parcel demand value.
Age structure can inform housing/service demand context, but local-authority age shares do not describe residents of an individual candidate parcel.
ONS publishes population density with local-authority estimates. Density is an area context signal and cannot establish achievable site density or capacity.
Births, deaths and migration components explain area growth. They remain historic/current demographic evidence and not a parcel-specific forecast.
Admin-based estimates can crosscheck demographic direction but methodology/status must be preserved and differences must not be silently reconciled.
Boundary vintages and geography codes must match the candidate's current authority before comparisons or trends are calculated.
SNPPs indicate possible future population under demographic assumptions; they are projections, not forecasts, and do not incorporate unobserved policy/development aims.
Projected children, working-age and older populations can inform service demand, but local-authority projections are not site-specific occupier forecasts.
ONS provides migration variants and corrected affected files. Variant choice must be explicit; no single projection is treated as certain future demand.
Projected births/deaths help explain demographic growth but remain assumption-driven area context, not parcel evidence.
Household projections are the latest official local-authority projections and a planning input; they are not a forecast of homes that should or will be built.
Projected household types can inform unit-mix context but cannot determine candidate scheme mix without market, policy and design evidence.
Projection uncertainty rises with horizon and smaller areas. Long-range values are never promoted as precise site demand.
IMD25 is the official relative deprivation measure for 33,755 LSOAs. Candidate use requires exact LSOA binding; it is not a parcel or individual attribute.
Income deprivation is neighbourhood context. Domain scores/ranks must retain their interpretation and cannot be converted to property value or resident income.
Employment deprivation is an LSOA-level relative measure and does not establish employment prospects or occupier demand for a candidate site.
Education deprivation can contextualise local social conditions but is distinct from school proximity, school quality and capacity.
Health deprivation is an area index, not a clinical or health-service-capacity measure and not a health claim about candidate residents.
The IMD crime domain is a composite small-area index and must remain separate from monthly Police.uk street-level records.
Barriers to Housing and Services and Living Environment are relative area domains; they cannot be read as exact parcel constraints or affluence measures.
Police.uk supports lat/lng street-level crime queries within about one mile. Published locations are anonymised approximations, so results are neighbourhood context only.
Crimes-at-location resolves lat/lng to a predefined anonymised location. It must not be represented as an incident occurring on the parcel.
Police.uk deliberately anonymises sensitive crime coordinates. Exact incident-to-parcel attribution is prohibited by the source semantics.
Valid categories depend on dataset date and current availability. Candidate comparisons must use the same month/category window.
Outcome data can contextualise recorded crimes but outcomes and crime records are time-dependent and must not become a parcel safety score without an approved model.
A single month can be volatile. Any future trend use must preserve availability, force coverage, anonymisation and consistent time windows.
Ofsted publishes school-level inspection data. Exact school URN/location binding is required before inspection outcomes are associated with candidate accessibility.
The renewed framework from November 2025 uses evaluation-area outcomes; legacy overall-grade comparisons must not be mixed without explicit framework handling.
Inspection data must be matched to the current establishment/URN and open status; predecessor/successor records must not be silently merged.
Safeguarding standards and categories of concern are inspection outcomes, not school capacity or admission availability.
Latest-inspection management data are updated frequently and official statistics can be provisional/revised; retrieval/publication dates must be retained.
CQC API/directory lists regulated locations including hospitals, GPs, dentists and care homes. Exact active location/address match is required for proximity.
Service types and specialisms distinguish what a registered location provides. A nearby CQC location is not interchangeable with a needed service.
Latest ratings may be location- or service-level and some multi-service locations are not rated at location level. Rating granularity must be preserved.
Active/inactive and registration start/end dates must be checked so archived or re-registered services are not counted as current capacity.
CQC notes system-migration delays and dual registrations in directory data. Exact current service capacity cannot be inferred from a directory row alone.

batches.t: Public EV charger local-authority context gate
batches.c: DfT official statistics provide charger counts by geography. Local-authority totals are context, not proof of an operational charger near the candidate.
Standard, standard-plus, rapid and ultra-rapid power bands serve different use cases. Candidate utility requires exact charger location, power and current availability.

batches.t: Transport Geography Portal nearest-charger query prep
batches.c: DfT states public charging data are available in standard geographies through its portal. Exact nearest charger must be resolved from current spatial data, not regional totals.
Public Charge Point Regulations require open data, but DfT warns portal spatial data may lag the latest publication. Dataset vintage must be retained.
LFB incident records provide where/when/type information and coordinate-level data. Historical incident occurrence is not a site fire-risk prediction.
Mobilisation records include appliance deployment and arrival timings. Past response performance does not guarantee future response time for a development.
Station areas are administrative/mobilising geographies and changed after 2014 closures. Exact current deployment origin cannot be inferred from historic station-area membership.
LFB rolling maps provide borough/ward incident context. Aggregated incident counts and rolling windows remain area context, not parcel-level hazard evidence.
